scope: Local complete production copy, server 1, date_start=2026-10-04
method: Five alternating warm-cache trials. Baseline SQL uses the original single-column indexes to reproduce the measured original plans.
changes: Composite indexes for measure(server_id,created_at), measure_app(measure_id,created_at), measure_disk(measure_id,created_at)
Application statistics compare timestamps directly and use an exclusive next-day bound for date_end
Long charts retain representative extrema and endpoints with a 2000-point maximum per series
Count-based retention uses small autocommitted batches and pauses; hourly scheduled runs cannot overlap
Native VACUUM is available through the existing manual maintenance command; daily automatic vacuum was removed
The representative-points message and its translations were removed

validation.schedule: Both hourly commands and retention mutex verified with an array test cache. Native schedule:list cannot inspect the unavailable local Redis socket.

resolved_findings.finding: Long ranges return every point without aggregation or a point budget
resolved_findings.resolution: Charts stream rows and retain at most 2000 points per series, preserving segment minima and maxima and the first and last point. Short ranges retain every point.
resolved_findings.measurement_note: PHP heap allocation excludes SQLite file-backed mmap pages and is not total process RSS. Streaming reduces payload and PHP memory; this long-range service trial takes more server CPU time.

resolved_findings.finding: Retention is a count per server and uses a single cascade DELETE, which can hold the SQLite writer lock during large cleanup
resolved_findings.resolution: Count-based retention is preserved. Deletes run in batches of at most 250 parent measures with a 200ms pause between batches. The hourly scheduled command uses Laravel withoutOverlapping.
resolved_findings.validation: A separate SQLite writer succeeds between each batch; foreign key cascades, retained records and other servers are preserved.

resolved_findings.finding: PRAGMA vacuum does not compact the database; fixture remained 2056192 bytes and native VACUUM reduced it to 8192 bytes. Real compaction requires a maintenance window
resolved_findings.resolution: The existing sqlite:vacuum command executes native VACUUM. Daily automatic vacuum was removed; compaction is manual during maintenance because it blocks writes.
resolved_findings.validation: The actual Artisan command reduces a temporary database file, preserves remaining rows, and passes quick_check.
